summary: All three published 2026 CBAM certificate prices and their publication dates match the workbook. Q4 2026 is NOT published and cannot exist before 16-18 Nov 2026. It is a whole-quarter average of EU ETS auction clearing prices (Q4 runs 1 Oct to 31 Dec 2026). The Commission calculates it in the first calendar week of the following quarter (28 Dec 2026 to 3 Jan 2027). It then publishes on the first working day of the next week, and its table shows Monday 4 January 2027 with the price cell blank. The certificate-sale start (1 Feb 2027) and first declaration/surrender date (30 Sep 2027) are verified in the legal text and have not changed since the workbook. I also reproduced the Q1-Q3 prices to the cent from EEX auction data, which independently confirms the method. The latest verifiable EUA auction clearing price is EUR 85.10 per tCO2 on 20 Oct 2026. No Q4 price was assumed anywhere. Outputs are in D:/Workspace/inter-trade-present/data/policy_status/cbam_price/ (README.md, CSV tables, raw/ responses, scripts/build_tables.py).

key_facts.label: Q1 2026 CBAM certificate price
key_facts.value: EUR 75.36 per tCO2e, published 7 April 2026 (EEX recomputation 75.3641)

key_facts.label: Q2 2026 CBAM certificate price
key_facts.value: EUR 75.28 per tCO2e, published 6 July 2026 (EEX recomputation 75.2766). Trade press that says 6 June is wrong.

key_facts.label: Q3 2026 CBAM certificate price
key_facts.value: EUR 82.32 per tCO2e, published 5 October 2026 (EEX recomputation 82.3185); Commission page dateModified 2026-10-05

key_facts.label: Q4 2026 CBAM certificate price status
key_facts.value: NOT PUBLISHED. Commission table lists publication date 4 January 2027 with an empty price cell. No price exists or may be assumed.

key_facts.label: Legal rule for 2026 quarterly price timing
key_facts.value: The Commission calculates a quarter's price during the first calendar week of the following quarter (IR 2025/2548 Art 1(2)) and publishes it on the first working day of the next calendar week (Art 4(1)). Basis: volume-weighted average of auction clearing prices of all auctions in the quarter, rounded to the cent. It applies to certificates for goods imported in that quarter.

key_facts.label: Q4 2026 calculation and publication window
key_facts.value: Quarter ends Thu 31 Dec 2026; calculation week Mon 28 Dec 2026 to Sun 3 Jan 2027; publication Mon 4 Jan 2027. This reading reproduces all three published dates, and 4 Jan matches the Commission table. The 16-18 Nov presentation falls inside Q4; the last scheduled 2026 EEX auctions are 14 Dec (CAP3), 11 Dec (DE), 9 Dec (PL).

key_facts.label: Weekly prices from 2027
key_facts.value: From 1 Jan 2027 the price is calculated every calendar week and published on the first working day of the calendar week following the relevant auctions (IR 2025/2548 Arts 5 and 8; Reg 2023/956 Art 21(1)-(2)).

key_facts.label: CBAM certificate sales start
key_facts.value: 1 February 2027 (Reg 2023/956 Art 20(1), as replaced by Reg 2025/2083). The Commission price page says all certificates are bought on the common central platform from February 2027. No change since the workbook.

key_facts.label: First CBAM declaration and certificate surrender
key_facts.value: 30 September 2027, for the year 2026 (Reg 2023/956 Art 6(1) and Art 22(1)); the Commission news item of 30 Sep 2026 repeats 30 September 2027 as the first compliance deadline. No change since the workbook.

key_facts.label: Latest EUA auction clearing price (context)
key_facts.value: EUR 85.10 per tCO2 on 20 Oct 2026 (EEX common platform CAP3, 2,791,500 EUAs). Same-month range on CAP3: 82.60 (5 Oct) to 87.04 (13 Oct). German platform 16 Oct: 85.50. This is context, not the CBAM price.

key_facts.label: EEX recomputation of Q1-Q3 prices
key_facts.value: Volume-weighted averages of all EEX auctions (CAP3+DE+PL+NI) give 75.3641, 75.2766 and 82.3185. These round to 75.36, 75.28 and 82.32 and match the Commission to the cent; CAP3-only or unweighted means do not match.

key_facts.label: Quarter-to-date October auctions (information only, NOT a Q4 price)
key_facts.value: Volume-weighted average of the 14 auctions of 1-20 Oct 2026 is 85.28 (32,296,500 allowances). A partial-quarter figure that must not be shown as Q4.

discrepancies_vs_workbook: No numerical discrepancy: Dataset E (Q1 75.36 on 7 Apr, Q2 75.28 on 6 Jul, Q3 82.32 on 5 Oct 2026) is confirmed on the live Commission table, and the workbook statement that Q4 was not yet published is still true on 22 Oct 2026.

New detail the workbook lacks: the Commission table now shows the Q4 2026 publication date as 4 January 2027 (price cell empty). The workbook and outline only say it was 'not yet published' and the outline lists 'Q4 2026 certificate price' under 'refresh before presenting'. That refresh cannot happen: no Q4 price will exist until 4 Jan 2027, after the 16-18 Nov presentation.

New detail the workbook lacks: the 2026 quarterly price applies by the quarter in which goods are imported (IR 2025/2548 Art 1(6)), not by the purchase or surrender date. The workbook's Q1 worked example is therefore correct only for goods imported in Q1 2026.

Sales start 1 Feb 2027 and first declaration/surrender 30 Sep 2027 are confirmed. The workbook's earlier-draft deadlines are not involved, and the final law (Reg 2025/2083) uses 30 Sep, not the 31 Aug 2027 or 31 May 2027 mentioned in older trade coverage of the Feb 2025 proposal.

The Commission's own page for the workbook's [S8]/[U35] source is https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism/price-cbam-certificates_en. The tempting URL .../cbam-certificate-prices_en returns HTTP 404, so cite the former.

caveats: Direct EUR-Lex URLs return an empty HTTP 202 (bot challenge) to scripted clients; I did not bypass it. Legal texts were taken from the Publications Office Cellar endpoint, which serves the Official Journal XHTML of the same acts. The consolidated 2023/956 (20.10.2025) is a documentation tool without legal effect, so Arts 6, 20, 21, 22 were also read in the amending Regulation 2025/2083 itself.

The 4 January 2027 date is the Commission's published schedule, backed by the legal timing rule and by a reading that reproduces all three published dates. The 'first calendar week' interpretation (Monday-Sunday week containing the quarter's first day) is mine. The explanation of the 7 April publication via Easter Monday is also an inference.
The 30 Sep 2026 Commission factsheet 'How CBAM certificates work' redirects to a DOI that would not load, so it was not used. The news item of the same date was used for 30 September 2027.

Last 2026 auction dates (CAP3 14 Dec, DE 11 Dec, PL 9 Dec) come from the EEX press release of 28 Jul 2025; the 2026 revisions say other auction details are unchanged, but I did not open the full dated EEX calendar.
The EEX file covers only EEX-run auctions; because Q1-Q3 reproduce to the cent, no other platform appears to carry material 2026 volume.

Searched for, and did not find, any act changing the 1 Feb 2027 or 30 Sep 2027 dates; the Commission legislation page (modified 2026-09-24) lists none after Reg 2025/2083. This is absence of evidence, not a legal-database certainty.
The Art 22(2) quarterly 50 percent holding rule is read as applying to goods imported from 2027; this is my reading of the wording and is not needed for the slides.
Trade press (alcircle, Andersen, GMK, Eurometal) was used only to find leads and never as the source of a figure.
